_comment: Guided tour for the QuEst card. Steps point at real controls; the ones with an await wait until the user presses the control.

steps.title: What QuEst simulates
steps.text:
A dye tethered to a protein by a flexible linker wanders over the surface; where it meets a quenching residue (tryptophan, tyrosine, histidine, methionine) its fluorescence can be quenched by photo-induced electron transfer (PET), and with a second dye it can also transfer energy by FRET. QuEst simulates that diffusion from the structure alone and gives you the decay you would measure.

Six steps; you press the buttons, the tour only points at them.

steps.title: Choose the structure
steps.text: Press Load PDB... and pick a structure. A valid attachment site (chain, residue, atom) is chosen for you; change it in Structure below.

await.hint: Press Load PDB... and choose a file.

steps.title: Describe the dye
steps.text: Under Dye set the linker length and width and the dye radius: they define where the dye can be (the accessible volume). Simulation sets the unquenched lifetime, the diffusion coefficient and how many photons to simulate.

steps.title: Simulate
steps.text: Press Simulate. The state line shows the quantum yield and the mean lifetime when it is done; Cancel discards the run.

steps.title: Read the decay
steps.text: The Plots & Dynamics tab shows the simulated fluorescence decay, the dye's distance from its mean position over the trajectory and how fast the dye forgets where it was (the autocorrelation).

steps.title: The chemistry
steps.text: Quenching Chemistry lists the quenching rate, contact radius, atoms and stickiness of each amino acid. They are the reference values; edit a cell to test another assumption.

steps.title: Save the project
steps.text: Save project... writes the form as a project file: the same file the QuEst command line and web interface read. Press Help for the parameters.
